<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913707_theRebbe_562" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913707_theRebbe_562__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening heading and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B'Siyata Dishmaya.</t>
    <t s="1">Monday of Rosh HaShanah, 5723.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse and the Targum's interpretation, questioning why the Holy Temple is called "the pride of Yaakov" and how it relates to our inheritance.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"He will choose our inheritance for us, the pride of Yaakov, whom He loves forever."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings in his maamar beginning with this discourse</t>
    <t s="2">(in the continuation of Rosh HaShanah 5703)</t>
    <t s="3">the translation of the Targum,</t>
    <t s="4">"He will choose for us to inherit our inheritance, the Temple of Yaakov, which He loves forever."</t>
    <t s="5">And he makes a precise point about this:</t>
    <t s="6">Behold, the Holy Temple belongs to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="7">"And they shall make for Me a Sanctuary"</t>
    <t s="8">[for Israel only builds the Sanctuary,</t>
    <t s="9">but the Sanctuary itself belongs to the Holy One, blessed be He].</t>
    <t s="10">So why is it called "the Temple of Yaakov"?</t>
    <t s="11">Also,</t>
    <t s="12">what is the connection of "the pride of Yaakov," which refers to the Holy Temple, to "our inheritance"?</t>
    <t s="13">And he explains in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="14">that "our inheritance" is the point of Judaism that dwells in the point of the heart, which is the "Temple of Yaakov,"</t>
    <t s="15">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="16">"And they shall make for Me a Sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst,"</t>
    <t s="17">"in it" is not said, but rather "in their midst,"</t>
    <t s="18">within each and every one of Israel.</t>
    <t s="19">And behold, the simple explanation of "He will choose for us... the pride of Yaakov" is,</t>
    <t s="20">that in the future He will return our Holy Temple to us.</t>
    <t s="21">And one must understand the connection between the explanation</t>
    <t s="22">(in the maamar)</t>
    <t s="23">that "the pride of Yaakov" refers to the Holy Temple within each and every one of Israel, and the explanation</t>
    <t s="24">(the simple one)</t>
    <t s="25">that "the pride of Yaakov" refers to the Third Holy Temple that will be built speedily in our days.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the connection of this Psalm to the Shofar blasts, describing how the Shofar transforms Divine judgment into mercy.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, this verse is in the Psalm that is recited seven times before the Shofar blast,</t>
    <t s="2">and the connection of this Psalm to the Shofar blast</t>
    <t s="3">(simply)</t>
    <t s="4">is,</t>
    <t s="5">for in this Psalm</t>
    <t s="6">it is stated, "God has ascended with a blast, the L-rd with the sound of the Shofar,"</t>
    <t s="7">and our Sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="8">that at first the Holy One, blessed be He, sits</t>
    <t s="9">(and ascends)</t>
    <t s="10">upon the Throne of Judgment,</t>
    <t s="11">"God has ascended with a blast,"</t>
    <t s="12">and by means of Israel taking their Shofars and blowing before the Holy One, blessed be He, He rises from the Throne of Judgment and sits upon the Throne of Mercy,</t>
    <t s="13">"the L-rd with the sound of the Shofar,"</t>
    <t s="14">and He is filled</t>
    <t s="15">with mercy for them, and has mercy upon them, and turns for them the attribute of judgment into mercy.</t>
    <t s="16">Therefore, we recite this Psalm before the Shofar blast in order to bring a proof from the Torah</t>
    <t s="17">regarding the drawing down</t>
    <t s="18">(of His rising from the Throne of Judgment and sitting upon the Throne of Mercy)</t>
    <t s="19">that is brought about by the Shofar blast.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
